title: Option Volume During Global Trading Hours Continues to Build
summary: Cboe Global Markets, a leading provider of market infrastructure and tradable products, delivers cutting-edge trading, clearing and investment solutions to market participants around the world.
body_markdown:
Options trading in extended hours has grown every week since the new Global Trading Hours (GTH) and Curb sessions[launched](https://www.cboe.com/insights/posts/gth-week-one-volume-builds-and-cboe-leads-on-market-share) on October 19 for 24 single stocks and five ETFs. Industry volume in the sessions rose from about 180,000 contracts in week one to 423,000 in week two, more than 1.5 million in week three and a record 2.09 million in week four. Average Daily Volume (ADV) climbed from roughly 36,000 contracts at launch to 418,000 in week four. That is still only about 1.7% of the ADV in these products, which leaves ample room to grow. Cboe data shows a widening mix of brokers and clearing firms offering the sessions to clients, and larger block trades point to early institutional use. Market quality, in terms of bid-ask spread and displayed size, has also improved across the products.


## Average Daily Volume

*Source: Cboe*


## Highlights


- **Session Breakdown:** Over the first month, the GTH session (7:30 am-9:25 am ET) has made up more than 82% of the overall GTH and Curb activity for non-index.
- **Product Mix:** On most days, ETF options made up 60 to 80% of the session volume, but NVDA has dominated recently.
- **Volume:** Daily volume has increased steadily since inception, with average daily volume for the latest week near 420,000 contracts and single day highs near 700,000 contracts.
- **Cboe Leads:** Over the first four weeks, Cboe executed 57% of the GTH volume and 51.15% of the combined GTH and Curb session volume.
- **Total Premium:** Over $1.4 billion has been transacted in the new sessions over the first four weeks.

Internal data shows the field of participants active during GTH and Curb hours on Cboe has doubled from 20 to 40 over since launch. Based on participation during regular trading hours, another 20 to 30 participants have yet to connect. Cboe derivative sales actively works with member firms and service providers to answer questions and facilitate connectivity.


## Market Quality: Single Stock Options Improve


While initial days saw the highest volume and tightest quotes in the most liquid ETFs, single stock market quality was inconsistent. As participation and volume have increased in recent weeks, quotes have tightened and displayed sizes have improved notably in single stock names.


**Exhibit 4: AAPL GTH Average Bid-Ask Spread and Displayed Size**


*Source: Cboe*


## Institutional Blocks


**Exhibit 5: NVDA Curb Session Blocks 11/5/26**


*Source: Cboe LiveVol Pro 11/5/26*


NVDA has seen high volatility and heavy option volume in recent days, with ADV rising from 2.8 million contracts in October to more than 5.1 million in November. Institutional activity outside of regular trading hours is evident in a number of large blocks that traded during the Curb session on November 5 involving nearly $68 million in total premium. These 480,432 contracts made up almost 10% of the regular trading hours activity on that date.


## What’s Next


The listed options market set a new single-day volume record this month, with more than 112 million contracts trading on November 5. Global Trading Hours and Curb sessions set daily records that week, with over 690,000 index options trading in the existing 8:15pm ET through 9:25am session, and nearly 700,000 of the newly available single stock and ETF contracts changing hands. While the trend toward longer trading hours dates back several decades in broad-based index derivatives, recent developments in risk assets made traders more comfortable with round-the-clock trading, and the options industry has taken care to select the most liquid, widely traded products for the new sessions. The 29 symbols listed are household names to most investors and make up nearly 60% of the market-wide option volume. As new brokers continue to roll out the sessions to clients, and new and existing liquidity providers expand operations, we anticipate continued strength in the segment, innovations in the marketplace, and an accelerated pace of growth for the industry.
